traceability.notes:
The 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION story is fully implemented.
All specified requirements are clearly mapped to code via JSDoc annotations and supporting helpers: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION and REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION are implemented by the valid-annotation-format rule and its create/Program/validation functions, which define and apply strict format rules for @story and @req annotations. - REQ-PATH-FORMAT and REQ-REQ-FORMAT are realized through default regex patterns in valid-annotation-options.ts and enforced in validateStoryAnnotation/validateReqAnnotation. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT and REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING are implemented by normalizeCommentLine, PendingAnnotation handling, collapseAnnotationValue, and processComment/processCommentLine, allowing multiline, styled JSDoc, and varied whitespace. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY is satisfied by buildStoryErrorMessage/buildReqErrorMessage and the rule’s messages.invalidStoryFormat/invalidReqFormat, all verified by tests that assert exact error messages.
Acceptance criteria are met: - Core Functionality: Rule validates @story/@req syntax and format as required. - Quality Standards: Implementation follows ESLint best practices, with meta, schema, tests via RuleTester, and inclusion in presets. - Integration: The rule works alongside function and branch annotation rules by scanning all comments; config integration tests confirm wiring. - User Experience & Error Handling: Errors are clear and specific, with detailed messages and safe auto-fix for common @story suffix issues; extensive tests cover malformed comments and edge cases. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents the format rules, default patterns, configuration, and examples aligned with the story.
Given the concrete implementation, comprehensive test coverage (all passing), and aligned documentation, the story’s functionality is complete and behaves as specified.
